text: Facilitation [Lat. facilis , easy]: Ger. Bahnung ; Fr. facilitation ; Ital. facilitazione , agevolezza . Increased ease of function, or of disposition for it, resulting from stimulation of any sort. It is one of the marks of the growth of HABIT (q.v., also for literature). The term has been given technical meaning as a translation of the German Bahnung (in neurology), which latter carries the idea of the preferential determination of a function, relatively to other functions, as to its pathway of discharge. Cf. TITCHENER, Amer. J. of Psychol., vii. 80. For cognate terms in psychology, see EXERCISE, HABITUATION, and PREPARATION. ( J.M.B .- G.F.S. )
